title: HINT for Financial Analysts — models stay sourced
metaDescription: Keep model inputs, formulas, scenarios, sensitivities and checks together so assistants never fill financial gaps with plausible figures.
h1: Your assistant builds models fast. HINT keeps every figure sourced.
intro: HINT keeps inputs, formulas, dates, scenarios and checks in plain-text notes beside a financial model. Your assistant sees which assumptions may change and which figures require an approved source.

situations.before: A blank rate becomes a plausible market assumption.
situations.body: The assistant asks for a dated source instead of filling the cell with a number that merely looks reasonable.

situations.before: A downside case changes both assumptions and formulas.
situations.body: Core calculation logic stays stable so scenario comparisons remain meaningful.

situations.before: A model balances because an error was hidden in a hard-coded value.
situations.body: Required reconciliations and tolerances travel with the output and cannot be smoothed over in commentary.

example.intro: The Bluth Finance demo grounds a Banana Stand model input in SRC-1.
example.after: It preserves the source and date, changes only inputs allowed by the scenario, and reports any failed model check.
example.compiled:
<input name="banana-stand-1">
  Approved input grounded in SRC-1.
</input>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: Invent a figure, rate, comparable or baseline.
Change a formula when a scenario permits only input changes.
Hide a failed check or unresolved reconciliation.
disclaimer: HINT supports model documentation and assistant context. It does not provide investment advice, valuation assurance or approval to rely on an output.

faq.a: No. HINT records model rules and sources; it does not recommend securities or financial decisions.
Only through sources and tools you explicitly provide. HINT itself does not fetch or invent current values.
Yes. Scenarios can specify which declared inputs change while leaving formulas and checks fixed.

keywordDescriptions.model: Sets the purpose, owner and valuation date of a model.
keywordDescriptions.input: Records a sourced and dated model input.
keywordDescriptions.driver: Names an assumption that may vary in a scenario.
keywordDescriptions.formula: Defines an explicit calculation from named inputs.
keywordDescriptions.output: Names a result and how it should be interpreted.
keywordDescriptions.scenario: Sets a coherent group of allowed input changes.
keywordDescriptions.sensitivity: Varies one declared driver over a stated range.
keywordDescriptions.check: Defines a reconciliation or tolerance that must pass.
